title: Network Discovery Reconciliation: Find What Your Records Miss

cta.text: See Micetro check your own network

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Network Discovery Reconciliation: Find What Your Records Miss".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "Find what your records miss" and whose text is exactly: Watch BlueCat Micetro 26.2 check your network against your records, and show you the devices nobody recorded and the records nobody can find.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
11 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. These are the networks Micetro found by managing your existing DNS and DHCP servers, such as Microsoft DNS, BIND and Microsoft DHCP. Micetro has not yet checked them against what the network actually sees.
2. Open the Action menu on the network and choose Set discovery schedule.
3. Switch on discovery for a network. Micetro checks every address in it on a schedule and notes who answers.
4. Every change carries a ticket number, so there is a record of who switched discovery on and why.
5. A few minutes later, open the network to see what answered.
6. This address answers, and Micetro has seen it. But it has no DNS name, no DHCP entry and no device behind it. Nobody recorded it.
7. Micetro ships with a report for devices it found by discovery. We make a working copy and leave the original alone.
8. One report lists every device that answered but has no record. These are the devices that are not recorded in your IPAM.
9. The second shipped report, IP reconciliation, lists records that no longer match what answers on the network.
10. Now the opposite check: machines your records say exist, but Micetro has not heard from lately. We shorten the time window so you can see it today.
11. This machine is in your records, but Micetro marks it as lost. It was last seen at 02:59. That is a record to check or clean up. Your records say one thing. The network says another. Micetro shows you the gap.
